results.summary_before: The Reactive Plasma CMOS Inverter is an educational hardware visualizer that generates a 640x480 VGA signal to illustrate the operation of a CMOS NOT gate. It displays a transistor-level schematic, a live oscilloscope waveform, and an active truth table, all driven by an internal frame counter. The design also produces a PWM audio tone that changes pitch with the input state. It requires a 25.175 MHz clock and a VGA monitor, with optional audio output, and is notable for being a demoscene entry that visualizes fundamental CMOS behavior entirely in logic gates.

results.summary_before: This design combines a Bernoulli stochastic multiplier, a conventional 4x4 unsigned multiplier, and a leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron on a single tile. The stochastic multiplier uses two LFSRs to generate random thresholds and estimates the product of two 4-bit probabilities over a window of cycles, while the conventional multiplier provides an exact product for comparison. The LIF neuron is a signed 8-bit integer model with configurable threshold, reset, and decay, and outputs a spike and membrane potential. The design is selected via two project select pins and requires no external hardware.

results.summary_before: This Verilog project is an ultra-low-power controller for an energy harvesting system that evaluates two proprietary harvesting topologies (P and S) and switches to the one yielding more energy. It uses an external LTC2450 SPI ADC to measure capacitor voltages, outputs pulses to control external switches, and logs results over UART at 1200 baud. To fit within a Tiny Tapeout tile, it replaces hardware multipliers with a custom 17-cycle shift-and-add sequential multiplier and runs at 32.768 kHz to minimize power. The design requires external harvesting circuitry, a USB-to-UART adapter, and an RTC oscillator for standalone operation, and is intended for academic research.

results.summary_before: This is a SystemVerilog implementation of the Snake game rendered over a 640x480 VGA interface, with an 8x8 tile gameboard and a rainbow-colored snake. The snake is stored in a 20-tile shift register, which caps its maximum length at 20 and the score at 99 due to limited BCD digit space. Five buttons control start and direction, and optional LEDs show current button presses. It requires a TinyVGA Pmod, a VGA monitor, and buttons or a joystick.

results.summary_before: DOTTEE is a demoscene demo that generates VGA graphics and audio, racing the beam to produce a 640x480 60fps output with music synthesized via a 1-bit sigma-delta DAC. It renders an array of colored circles using distance calculations and constructs a 'DOTTEE' logo with a Tiny Tapeout-inspired 'TT'. The demo loops after 4096 frames and includes a noise generator for percussive sounds. It requires a Tiny VGA PMOD and a TT Audio PMOD for output, and is notable for its efficient 1-tile implementation and participation in the Tiny Tapeout Demoscene Competition.

results.summary_before: This project displays a bouncing ball on a 640x480 VGA screen, with position and velocity controlled via SPI commands. The SPI receiver decodes one-byte commands where the upper two bits select the parameter and the lower six bits provide the value, with velocity clamped to -10 to 10 and position updated every six video frames. It is tested using a cocotb testbench that sends SPI commands and checks movement, clamping, reset, and edge rebound behavior. The design requires a TinyVGA-style PMOD for output and an SPI master for command input, and it is notable for its simple physics engine and live pixel rendering without a framebuffer.
